title: LiPLUS Holdings says unauthorized access to Widsley's Telforce calling system may have exposed 約28万件 of records
date_note: Date of LiPLUS Holdings' own notice; ScanNetSecurity reported it on 26 November. Widsley reported the access to LiPLUS on 21 October.
summary: LiPLUS Holdings' notice says Widsley, which supplies the Telforce cloud calling system, reported unauthorized access from overseas on 21 October. A third-party investigator found information may have been taken through a route that left no access record. The notice says 約28万件 of records, including phone numbers, may have leaked; leakage is not confirmed and no secondary harm has been confirmed.
plain: A calling system used by LiPLUS was accessed from overseas. The company says 約28万件 of records with phone numbers and other details may have leaked; it has not confirmed a leak.
exec: LiPLUS says 約28万件 of records may have leaked via a supplier's calling system.
action: LiPLUS advises that it never asks for passwords, card or account numbers by phone, SMS or email, and that people should not open URLs or attachments in unexpected messages.
geo_basis: company location not stated in the pages read; country-level marker at Tokyo

evidence.quote: 約28万件の電話番号、名前（登録がある場合）、住所（郵便番号のみの場合を含む）、会社名、問い合わせ内容等の記録、通話日時を含む個人情報

validation.note: LiPLUS Holdings' own notice (primary) and ScanNetSecurity each state the unauthorized access and the figure of 約28万件.

review.note: Compared date, Widsley 21 Oct report, 28man figure and quote, unconfirmed leak and advice against LiPLUS notice and ScanNetSecurity
